findings.practical_consequence: The atomic-duty mapping proves identifier ownership, not semantic coverage, and concrete duties are assigned to replacement clauses that do not contain them. Required correction: Replace owner-only atomic records with a semantic disposition for every duty: retain/revise/move/retire, preserved intent, exact replacement clause or downstream owner, activation and stop behavior, rationale for any narrowed or retired mechanic, and a test oracle. Resolve G0-M1 and G11-M1 explicitly, then validate semantic coverage rather than counts alone.
evidence: complete_atomic_inventory defines G0-M1 as the ordinary-task working-agreement trigger plus disclosure when higher authority prevents loading; complete_replacement_mapping assigns it to proposed G0, whose proposed text only requires a substantive-response anchor and forbids routine audits.

complete_atomic_inventory defines G11-M1 as a granular change-by-change plan with reasons and approval before editing; complete_replacement_mapping assigns it to proposed G7, whose proposed text gates paths and effects but contains no granular-plan, rationale, or wait-for-approval mechanism.
The directive-level disposition says G11 mechanics move to a playbook, but the atomic mapping still names proposed G7 and identifies no playbook clause or explicit retirement rationale.

findings.practical_consequence: The topology and adoption inventory omit playbook-convergence-loop even though current directives make it a direct authorization and blocker-lifecycle consumer. Required correction: Add the canonical and installed playbook-convergence-loop contracts to the exact consumer topology and evidence index; record parity, future ownership/disposition, required edits or an evidence-backed no-change decision, and adoption tests proving explicit invocation grants only envelope-bounded edits and cannot recreate recursive blocker remediation or external-effect authority.
evidence: Current G11-M2 grants special edit authority when playbook-convergence-loop is explicitly invoked, and G20-M3 requires blocker identity propagation through that loop.

skills/playbook-convergence-loop/SKILL.md independently defines its authorization envelope, mutable state, delegation, guarded edits, verification, and review-to-fix recursion, so its contract can duplicate or conflict with the replacement envelope and non-expansion rules.

candidate exact_topology, evidence_index, mode-playbook ownership, and verification-skill adoption inventory do not include the canonical playbook-convergence-loop skill or its installed managed copy; occurrences in the candidate are only reproduced current-duty text.

findings.practical_consequence: The deterministic scenario suite does not explicitly prove several frozen external-effect nonregressions. Required correction: Add deterministic positive and negative scenario/test oracles for commit, push, secret access, and external messages, each naming the envelope permission and owner, the exact permitted action or stop, and forbidden inference by lower directives, playbooks, sequences, or tools. Trace them into the adoption validation contract.
evidence: FUT-008 requires nonregression proving that no scenario gains authority to commit, push, access secrets, or send external messages, among the other enumerated protections.

The 17 deterministic scenario oracles include deploy, irreversible migration, dirty-tree, schema, and implicit-secret prohibitions, but contain no direct action-or-stop case for commit permission, push permission, external messaging, or an authorized-versus-unauthorized secret-access boundary.

The adoption test list says only "effect approvals"; it supplies no input boundary, expected action or stop, or forbidden behavior for those distinct approval classes, while candidate G7 merely declares the rule.
